t: Subject to section 502 of the Congressional Budget Act of 1974, during fiscal year 2013, obligations of direct loans may not exceed $24,000,000 for Individual Fishing Quota loans and not to exceed $59,000,000 for traditional direct loans as authorized by the Merchant Marine Act of 1936:  Provided, That none of the funds made available under this heading may be used for direct loans for any new fishing vessel that will increase the harvesting capacity in any United States fishery.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that loans to fishers bring outside parties into the picture, but receiving or applying for a loan is not participating in a federal decision. The section only caps direct loan obligations and bars using the funds for new fishing vessels that increase harvesting capacity. It requires no comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation with outside entities, rulemaking, or right to sue.
fable.s: obligations of direct loans may not exceed $24,000,000 for Individual Fishing Quota loans

qwen_block.w: This section is an appropriations provision that sets spending limits and restrictions on the use of funds for direct loans. It does not require consultation, coordination, or participation with any outside parties (such as states, tribes, or the public) before a decision is made. The reference to the Congressional Budget Act is internal to the federal government process.
qwen_block.s: Subject to section 502 of the Congressional Budget Act of 1974, during fiscal year 2013, obligations of direct loans may not exceed $24,000,000 for Individual Fishing Quota loans and not to exceed $59,000,000 for traditional direct loans as authorized by the Merchant Marine Act of 1936: Provided, That none of the funds made available under this heading may be used for direct loans for any new fishing vessel that will increase the harvesting capacity in any United States fishery.

opus.w: This is a spending provision that limits how much can be committed to fishing loan programs and restricts which vessels can receive loans. It does not require or allow consultation with anyone outside the federal government, a public hearing, a comment period, an advisory body, rulemaking, or a right to sue. The mention of loans does not count as participation, because applying for a loan or other benefit is excluded by the definition.
opus.s: obligations of direct loans may not exceed $24,000,000 for Individual Fishing Quota loans and not to exceed $59,000,000 for traditional direct loans as authorized by the Merchant Marine Act of 1936

qwen_chat.w: This section is an appropriations provision that sets spending limits and conditions on the use of funds for direct loans. It does not require or recommend any consultation, coordination, or participation with outside parties (such as fishermen, states, or the public) before making decisions. The restriction on loans for vessels that increase harvesting capacity is a substantive policy constraint applied by the agency, not a procedural requirement for external input.
qwen_chat.s: Subject to section 502 of the Congressional Budget Act of 1974, during fiscal year 2013, obligations of direct loans may not exceed $24,000,000 for Individual Fishing Quota loans and not to exceed $59,000,000 for traditional direct loans as authorized by the Merchant Marine Act of 1936: Provided, That none of the funds made available under this heading may be used for direct loans for any new fishing vessel that will increase the harvesting capacity in any United States fishery.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that the restriction on loans for new fishing vessels implies a consultation with fishermen or industry groups to determine if a vessel increases harvesting capacity. However, the text itself does not mandate any such consultation, hearing, or comment period. It simply sets a funding cap and a condition on the use of funds. The decision-making process described is internal to the agency (determining if a loan fits the criteria) and does not involve external participation as defined.
